attempts.upstream_source_modified: dead-include removals (ctype.h, string.h) only; verified semantics-preserving. All memcpy calls use __builtin_memcpy (compiler builtin, not libc). strings.h header note confirms ebpf code intentionally avoids libc string functions.

verdict: TripleCross does not build out of the box on Ubuntu 26.04 / kernel 7.0 with the project's pinned libbpf and clang 16+ toolchain. Even after removing provably dead libc includes (semantics-preserving build-env adaptation), the BPF stack limit is exceeded by kit.bpf.c's handler functions. Raising clang's -mllvm -bpf-stack-size would defer the failure to load time where the kernel verifier enforces the same limit. Taking the sample further would require non-trivial source refactoring (splitting XDP handlers, reducing on-stack buffers) which was out of scope.
scope_note: Only two kinds of patches were applied, both documented in BUILD_ENV_COMPAT_PATCH.json: removing an unused #include <ctype.h> and removing an unused #include <string.h>. Both are dead code (verified by grep for every function those headers would provide). No behavioral change. Rootkit logic is bit-identical.
